text.p: Australian retailing giant Coles Myer Ltd is expected to record a slump in profits for the year to July 31, reflecting margin pressure within a depressed retail environment, analysts said on Monday.

Analysts' average forecast for the company's net profit before abnormals and preference dividends was A$283 million, down 33 percent from a year earlier. Forecasts ranged between A$272 million and A$304 million. The company reports on Tuesday.

"A large part of it is just the difficult retail sales environment and they have been pursuing sales growth and that's cost them something in margins," said Macquarie Equities Ltd analyst Simon Shakeseff.
Coles Myer said in August that margin pressure and repositioning costs would hit its full-year results.
The warning came after its announcement of an 8.2 percent rise in full-year sales revenue to A$18.2 billion.

Analysts noted that the supermarkets division had accounted for most of the rise in sales while department stores, discount stores and toy store World 4 Kids had lagged and were expected to drag the bottom line lower.
"Down is the direction for all of the earnings areas except food," said one Melbourne-based analyst.

Operating profit for the Myer/Grace Bros department stores was expected to fall by about 30 percent from A$123.3 million in 1994/95 despite a strategy that intended to reposition them upmarket, Macquarie's Shakesheff said.
"They really seem to be, to some extent, still paying the price of underinvestment in the late 80s and early 90s ... They're just old and tired stores," he added.
Coles Myer's ailing toy division, World 4 Kids, was forecast to post a loss of between A$30 million and A$45 million, analysts said.
World 4 Kids, subject to intermittent speculation of its imminent closure, has been under review since mid-March.
Shakesheff said he would welcome the creation of a provision for the loss-making unit in the group's 1995/96 accounts.
"The provision would be a reasonable sum of money, upwards of A$30 million ... to cover costs of closing some of World 4 Kids and merging World 4 Kids with (discount chain) Kmart," he said.
